newsitem.title: USA: Fine Airlines plans Asia sales agent.
newsitem.headline: Fine Airlines plans Asia sales agent.

text.p: Fine Airlines Inc, the Miami-based all-cargo airline, will soon announce it has hired its first general sales agent (GSA) in Asia, a top officer told Reuters Friday.
"We are pending conclusion of GSA representation which would give us coverage in many Asian countries," Hugh Nash, vice president, said.
Fine, which carried the most international cargo through Miami International Airport last year, will have representation in at least 10 Asian countries, including China and Japan, Nash said.
He declined to name the agent or say when the announcement will be made.

Many transporation companies are trying to position themselves to take advantage of the increasing trade between Asia and Latin America. Miami based-companies such as Fine hope Miami will be the hub for such trade.

The privately-held Fine has been adding routes, representation and executives over the last few months. In the spring it inked a deal with general sales agent CAS Cargo & Travel Inc, Toronto, to represent Fine in Canada.

Also in the spring it hired Walter Colon, a former cargo manager with Iberia Airlines, to be its regional manager for the Northeast based at John F. Kennedy Airport in New York. Chuck Patton, who formerly had the JFK job, was moved to Atlanta to become the regional manager for the Southern region. This month Fine began flying to Brazil and increased its service to Guatamala.

Fine carried 163,179 tons of international cargo through MIA last year, ranking it number one. That was an increase of 10 percent over 1995 and accounted for about 11 percent of all international freight through MIA, according to statistics compiled by the Dade County Aviation Department.
